speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You've reported a headache and worsening vision over three weeks; to begin my assessment, could you describe the specific location, quality (e.g., throbbing, sharp), and severity of your pain on a scale of one to ten?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis).

Given your age, the three-week history of headache and worsening vision, and the absence of other systemic symptoms, I need to rule out an ophthalmic emergency immediately. Please report to the nearest emergency department immediately for an urgent eye examination and blood tests (ESR, CRP) to prevent permanent vision loss.
